lead.headline: Strive's $630M SATS IPO tests whether Bitcoin-tied vehicles can scale without promising actual Bitcoin
lead.tldr: Today's throughline is the widening gap between crypto-adjacent capital formation and on-chain fundamentals: Strive raises $630M on a Bitcoin-linked structure with unspecified allocation, while stablecoin transfer volumes quadruple to $891B on actual bank adoption, and exploiters still move freely with $194M in stolen ETH.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the distance between narrative and structure is becoming the key underwriting variable.

top_signals.title: Strive closes $630M SATS IPO, leaves Bitcoin allocation unspecified11m
top_signals.summary: Strive has successfully closed its SATS IPO, raising $630 million. While the offering is linked to Bitcoin, the specific allocation of the funds toward the asset remains unspecified.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The unspecified Bitcoin allocation in Strive's $630M raise signals that institutional capital is increasingly comfortable with crypto-adjacent risk exposure without requiring transparent on-chain backing, which reprices how we underwrite correlation risk in these vehicles.

top_signals.title: Stablecoin transfers quadruple to $891B as US banks expand adoption: Report17m
top_signals.summary: Stablecoin transfer volumes have surged to $891 billion, representing a fourfold increase. This growth is largely attributed to the expanding adoption of stablecoins by US banking institutions.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The fourfold surge to $891B in stablecoin transfers driven by US bank adoption is repricing stablecoin infrastructure as a core banking utility rather than a crypto-native novelty, shifting where we expect fee extraction and regulatory capture.

top_signals.title: Drift exploiter sends $61M ETH to Tornado Cash, holds $194M
top_signals.summary: An exploiter of the Drift protocol has moved $61 million in ETH to the mixer Tornado Cash after a two-month period of inactivity. The attacker is estimated to still hold approximately $194 million across linked addresses.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $61M Tornado Cash deposit from the Drift exploiter, with $194M still held, demonstrates that mixer sanctions remain structurally porous and that exploit recovery economics are deteriorating for protocols and their underwriters.

top_signals.title: Bitwise, Hyperliquid seek SEC rule changes for token trading, airdrops
top_signals.summary: Bitwise and Hyperliquid are petitioning the SEC for rule changes regarding token trading and airdrops. Legal experts are simultaneously challenging the SEC's authority to establish new exemptions in this space.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bitwise and Hyperliquid's joint SEC petition on token trading and airdrops, paired with legal challenges to the SEC's exemption authority, suggests the industry is moving from defensive compliance to proactive rulemaking—a higher-variance strategy that could accelerate or bifurcate the US market.

top_signals.title: Crypto firms, Wall Street push SEC to revise Regulation Crypto Assets as comments close
top_signals.summary: Crypto firms and Wall Street institutions are urging the SEC to revise the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets. The feedback focuses on the regulatory framework and the newly released innovation exemption.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The coordinated push from crypto and Wall Street on Regulation Crypto Assets' innovation exemption indicates that incumbent financial institutions now have sufficient skin in the game to lobby for rules that may entrench their position against native crypto competitors.

deals.summary: Strive has successfully closed its SATS IPO, raising $630 million. While the offering is linked to Bitcoin, the specific allocation of the funds toward the asset remains unspecified.

Mural, a startup founded by former Palantir engineers, has raised $15 million in a funding round led by Tether. The company focuses on connecting banks to the bot economy and managing cross-border payments across various currencies.
Bitget is planning to acquire a licensed cryptocurrency exchange operator in Thailand via BTG. This strategic expansion comes shortly after the company dealt with a significant $388M hack.

Nectar Group has raised $5 million at a $30 million valuation to launch HoneyB, a Bitcoin yield platform. The product will initially target institutional investors located outside of the United States.

on_the_radar.title: FINMA approves Switzerland’s first Bitcoin ETF for retail investors
on_the_radar.summary: The Swiss financial regulator FINMA has approved the first Bitcoin ETF available to retail investors in Switzerland. While granting approval, the regulator issued a warning regarding the high volatility associated with cryptocurrency assets.

on_the_radar.title: Swiss regulator FINMA approves country's first spot bitcoin ETF for retail investors
on_the_radar.summary: The Swiss financial regulator FINMA has approved the first spot Bitcoin ETF specifically for retail investors. While Switzerland previously had Bitcoin ETPs, this new product operates under a distinct regulatory framework for investment funds.

on_the_radar.title: BlackRock files for third Bitcoin ETF, still no Solana or XRP
on_the_radar.summary: BlackRock has filed for its third Bitcoin-related fund, the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF. The move comes amid market speculation regarding whether the asset manager will expand its ETF offerings to include Solana or XRP.

on_the_radar.title: BlackRock's IBIT Bitcoin ETF draws $665 million inflow, highest since October 2025
on_the_radar.summary: BlackRock's IBIT Bitcoin ETF experienced a significant surge in inflows totaling $665 million, marking its highest level since October 2025. Analysts suggest this may indicate investors are positioning for a 'catch-up trade' in Bitcoin.

on_the_radar.title: MoonPay, Upbit parent Dunamu explore collaboration on stablecoin payments, GIWA expansion
on_the_radar.summary: MoonPay and Dunamu, the parent company of Upbit, are exploring a collaboration focused on stablecoin payments. The partnership also aims to expand global access to Dunamu's Ethereum Layer 2 network, the GIWA chain.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto’s 2026 shutdown wave claims 82 projects. What went wrong? 25m
on_the_radar.summary: An analysis of the significant wave of project shutdowns in the crypto space leading into 2026, with 82 projects ceasing operations. The report examines the systemic failures and market conditions that led to these collapses.

on_the_radar.title: Injective, BDACS plan Korean won stablecoin settlement for tokenized assets
on_the_radar.summary: Injective has partnered with South Korea's BDACS to integrate the KRW1 stablecoin into tokenized asset markets. This collaboration aims to enable efficient settlement of tokenized assets using the Korean won.

on_the_radar.title: Alphabet, Microsoft add objections to OKX-ICE proposed tokenized stock platform32m
on_the_radar.summary: Alphabet and Microsoft have filed objections against a proposed tokenized stock platform developed by OKX and ICE. The tech giants are challenging the legal and regulatory framework of the initiative to bring traditional equities onto the blockchain.

worth_a_read.title: Aptos Tokenomics: Path to Deflation
worth_a_read.note: Aptos's path to deflationary tokenomics is worth tracking as a case study in whether Layer 1s can engineer sustainable value accrual without relying on emission-driven TVL growth.

worth_a_read.title: Solana Alpenglow
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's Solana Alpenglow research provides technical depth on Solana's next consensus iteration, which matters for repricing Solana's latency advantage against Ethereum L2s.

worth_a_read.title: Trading is now a video game with Legend
worth_a_read.note: The Legend trading-as-video-game thesis from Galaxy is relevant for understanding whether gamified interfaces are capturing genuine flow or just redistributing existing retail speculation with higher take rates.

linkedin_post:
Strive just raised $630 million for something called SATS. It is "linked to Bitcoin." The Bitcoin allocation? Unspecified.

We have seen this structure before. Closed-end funds, interval funds, now a SPAC-adjacent IPO wrapper. The pitch is directional Bitcoin exposure. The mechanics are opacity plus fee extraction. What is being underwritten is not Bitcoin's price. It is the willingness of allocators to buy a proxy they cannot fully inspect.

This is happening while actual stablecoin rails hit $891 billion in transfer volume. US banks are adopting. Settlement is moving on-chain. The contrast is sharp: one market builds infrastructure, the other sells narrative.

We do not know yet whether Strive's structure becomes a template or a caution. The test is simple. If the vehicle trades at persistent premium to its opaque underlying, the model replicates. If the premium collapses when Bitcoin volatility returns, allocators will have paid basis points for correlation they did not understand.

Our radar is on the second-order effect: whether this capital formation style crowds out direct custody solutions, or whether it simply educates the same allocators on why direct custody exists.

The $194 million still sitting in Drift exploiter wallets suggests we are not short on reasons to prefer inspectable structures.
